dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992
Overview
Enactment: By Parliament in the Forty-third Year of the Republic of India Commencement:
•	Sections 11 to 14 came into force at once.
•	Remaining provisions deemed to have come into force on 19th June, 1992.
Key Provisions 
1.	Powers of Central Government
•	Make Orders for developing and regulating foreign trade (Imports & Exports).
•	Prohibit, restrict, or regulate imports/exports of goods, services, or technology.
•	Formulate and announce Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) and amend it.
2.	Director General of Foreign Trade
•	Appointment by Central Government.
•	Advises on FTP formulation and is responsible for its implementation.
•	May be delegated certain powers by the Central Government.
3.	Definitions
•	Import/Export: Broadly defined for goods, services, and technology, with specific clauses for services and technology.
•	Services/Technology: Defined with clarity on what constitutes supply/import/export.
•	Other key definitions: Adjudicating Authority, Appellate Authority, Conveyance, etc.
4.	Regulatory Framework
•	Licenses: Not necessary unless required under this Act or its rules/orders.
•	Prohibitions/Restrictions: Goods under prohibition/regulation deemed so under the Customs Act, 1962.
•	Continuance of Existing Orders: Orders under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1947, continue unless inconsistent.
5.	Repeal and Savings
•	Repeals the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, 1947, and the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Ordinance, 1992.
•	Savings clause for previous operations, rights, and liabilities under the repealed Acts.
6.	Penalty, Confiscation, and Adjudication
•	Power of Search and Seizure (mentioned but details not provided in the context).
•	Contraventions: Lead to penalty/confiscation (details not provided).
•	Adjudicating Authority: Established for deciding on contraventions.
•	Owner's Opportunity: Right to be heard before action on seized goods.
